# Implement and run the synthetic historical control

The parcel's past is its comparison: blocks of its own earlier months are weighted to
reproduce its most recent months, and what followed those blocks becomes the forecast.
`references/method.md` describes the construction; every setting and every choice in it
is yours, made inside your program.

## Workflow

1. `python scripts/show_data.py` — the nine months, every band. The same data is in
   `data.csv` in this directory: one row per band per month, columns `band`, `period_id`
   (P01–P09 in time order), `month` (YYYY-MM), `mean_value`.
2. Read `references/method.md`. Decide how to build the blocks, what to match, how to fit
   and constrain the weights, how to select blocks, and how to form the prediction.
3. Write `predict.py`. It reads `data.csv` and prints one line per band, `BAND VALUE`, the
   predicted mean value for the next month. numpy, scipy and pandas are available; nothing
   outside this directory is, and there is no network.
4. Run `python predict.py`. Fix what fails; run again. Every run is recorded.
5. Finish by writing `answer.json`:
   ```json
   {"prediction": {"<band>": <value>, ...}, "rationale": "<what the program does and why>"}
   ```

# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.

import pandas as pd, numpy as np, itertools

df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')
w = df.pivot(index='period_id', columns='band', values='mean_value').sort_index()
bands = list(w.columns)
X = w.values  # 9 x 3
T = 9
m, n = 3, 1  # matching length, forward length
nb = T - m - n + 1  # number of blocks
# block i: matching months i..i+m-1, forward month i+m
M = np.array([X[i:i+m].ravel() for i in range(nb)])   # blocks x (m*3)
F = np.array([X[i+m] for i in range(nb)])             # blocks x 3 (first forward month)
target = X[T-m:].ravel()                              # matching window (last m months)

def fit(idx):
    A = M[list(idx)].T  # (m*3) x k
    sol, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(A, target, rcond=None)
    sol = np.clip(sol, 0, None)  # nonnegative weights
    sol /= sol.sum() if sol.sum() > 0 else 1
    err = np.mean((A @ sol - target)**2)
    return sol, err

best = None
for k in range(1, nb+1):
    for idx in itertools.combinations(range(nb), k):
        sol, err = fit(idx)
        if best is None or err < best[1]:
            best = (idx, sol, err)
idx, sol, err = best
pred = F[list(idx)].T @ sol
print("kept blocks:", idx, "weights:", np.round(sol,3), "match MSE:", err)
for b, v in zip(bands, pred):
    print(b, v)
EOF

# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.

# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.

# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.

# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.

# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.

steps.output:
# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.

import pandas as pd, numpy as np, itertools, json

df = pd.read_csv("data.csv")
w = df.pivot(index="period_id", columns="band", values="mean_value").sort_index()
bands = list(w.columns)
X = w.values  # 9 x B, time-ordered P01..P09

m, n = 3, 1          # matching length, forward length
nb = 9 - m - n + 1   # number of blocks
# block i: matching part X[i:i+m], forward part X[i+m:i+m+n]
M = np.array([X[i:i+m].ravel() for i in range(nb)])   # blocks x (m*B)
F = np.array([X[i+m:i+m+n].ravel() for i in range(nb)]) # blocks x (n*B)
target = X[9-m:].ravel()  # matching window = last m months

def fit(idx):
    A = M[list(idx)].T          # (m*B) x k
    coef, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(A, target, rcond=None)
    pred = A @ coef
    err = np.mean((pred - target)**2)
    return coef, err

best = None
for k in range(1, nb+1):
    for idx in itertools.combinations(range(nb), k):
        coef, err = fit(idx)
        if best is None or err < best[1]:
            best = (idx, coef, err)

idx, coef, err = best

           "weighted combination of the blocks' first forward months, as observed.")},

df = pd.read_csv("data.csv")

    coef, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(A, target, rcond=None)

# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.

bands = sorted(df.band.unique())
periods = [f"P{i:02d}" for i in range(1,10)]
months = [df[df.period_id==p].month.iloc[0] for p in periods]
Y = np.array([[df[(df.band==b)&(df.period_id==p)].mean_value.iloc[0] for p in periods] for b in bands])  # (B,9)
B = len(bands); T = 9
t = np.arange(1,10)

# --- preparation: remove annual sine/cosine after partialling out trend ---
X = np.column_stack([np.ones(T), t])  # trend
prep = np.zeros_like(Y)
seas = {}
for j in range(B):
    beta, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(X, Y[j], rcond=None)
    resid = Y[j] - X@beta
    # annual cycle: sin/cos of 2*pi*month/12
    mm = np.array([int(m[5:7]) for m in months])
    S = np.column_stack([np.sin(2*np.pi*mm/12), np.cos(2*np.pi*mm/12)])
    # regress resid on seasonal (after trend partialled out)
    Sd = S - X@np.linalg.lstsq(X, S, rcond=None)[0]
    g, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(Sd, resid, rcond=None)
    seas[bands[j]] = (g, beta)
    prep[j] = resid - Sd@g

# --- smoothing: local-linear Gaussian kernel, bandwidth h ---
h = 2.0
sm = np.zeros_like(prep)
for i in range(T):
    w = np.exp(-0.5*((t-t[i])/h)**2)
    A = np.column_stack([np.ones(T), t-t[i]])
    W = np.diag(w)
    coef = np.linalg.solve(A.T@W@A + 1e-8*np.eye(2), A.T@W@prep.T)
    sm[:,i] = coef[0]

# --- standardize each band over P01-P09 ---
mu = sm.mean(axis=1, keepdims=True)
sd = sm.std(axis=1, keepdims=True); sd[sd<1e-9]=1
Z = (sm-mu)/sd

# --- blocks: m=3 matching, n=1 forward ---
m, n = 3, 1
nb = T - m - n + 1  # 6
blocks = [Z[:, s:s+m] for s in range(nb)]
fwd = [Z[:, s+m] for s in range(nb)]  # first forward month in prepared space
target = Z[:, T-m:]  # P07-P09

def mse(w):
    comb = sum(wi*blocks[i] for i,wi in enumerate(w) if wi>0)
    return np.mean((comb-target)**2)

def fit(subset):
    A = np.stack([blocks[i].ravel() for i in subset], axis=1)
    b = target.ravel()
    # nonnegative least squares
    from scipy.optimize import nnls
    w, _ = nnls(A, b)
    return w, np.mean((A@w - b)**2)

# stepwise selection
best = None
cand = []
tol = 1e-4
cur = []
while True:

        sub = cur+[i]
        w, e = fit(sub)
        if beststep is None or e < beststep[1]: beststep = (sub, e, w)
    if beststep is None: break
    if best is None or beststep[1] < best[1] - tol:
        best = beststep[1]; cur, w = beststep[0], beststep[2]
        # re-fit weights for cur
        w, e = fit(cur); best = e

    else:

# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.

The parcel's past is its comparison: blocks of its own earlier months are weighted to

# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.

M = np.hstack([Z[:, b].ravel() for b in blocks])       # columns = blocks

best = None
for r in range(1, nb+1):
    for sub in itertools.combinations(range(nb), r):
        A = M[:, list(sub)]

        Aa = np.vstack([A, np.ones((1, A.shape[1]))*10])
        bvec = np.append(t, 10.0)

# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.

target = X[-m:]

mu, sd = X.mean(0), X.std(0)
T = ((target - mu)/sd).ravel()
B = [((b - mu)/sd).ravel() for b in blocks]

def fit(sub):
    A = np.stack([B[i] for i in sub], axis=1)
    # nonneg weights summing to 1: augment with large penalty row
    lam = 10.0
    Aa = np.vstack([A, lam*np.ones((1, len(sub)))])
    ya = np.concatenate([T, [lam]])
    w, _ = nnls(Aa, ya)
    s = w.sum()
    if s <= 0: return None, np.inf
    w = w/s
    err = np.mean((A@w - T)**2)
    return w, err

tol = 1e-4
kept, cur_err = [], np.inf
improved = True
while improved:
    improved = False
    best = None
    for i in range(nb):
        if i in kept: continue
        sub = kept + [i]
        w, err = fit(sub)
        if w is not None and (best is None or err < best[1]):
            best = (i, w, err)
    if best and best[2] < cur_err - tol:
        kept.append(best[0]); cur_err = best[2]; improved = True

import pandas as pd, numpy as np, itertools
from scipy.optimize import nnls

df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')
bands = sorted(df.band.unique())
periods = [f"P{i:02d}" for i in range(1,10)]
X = df.pivot(index='period_id', columns='band', values='mean_value').loc[periods, bands].values

m, n = 3, 1
nb = 9 - m - n + 1
blocks = [X[i:i+m] for i in range(nb)]
fwd = [X[i+m] for i in range(nb)]
target = X[-m:]

mu, sd = X.mean(0), X.std(0)
T = ((target - mu)/sd).ravel()
B = [((b - mu)/sd).ravel() for b in blocks]

def fit(sub):
    A = np.stack([B[i] for i in sub], axis=1)
    # nonneg weights summing to 1: augment with large penalty row
    lam = 10.0
    Aa = np.vstack([A, lam*np.ones((1, len(sub)))])
    ya = np.concatenate([T, [lam]])
    w, _ = nnls(Aa, ya)
    s = w.sum()
    if s <= 0: return None, np.inf
    w = w/s
    err = np.mean((A@w - T)**2)
    return w, err

# stepwise selection with tolerance
tol = 1e-4
kept, cur_err = [], np.inf
improved = True
while improved:
    improved = False
    best = None
    for i in range(nb):
        if i in kept: continue
        sub = kept + [i]
        w, err = fit(sub)
        if w is not None and (best is None or err < best[2]):
            best = (i, w, err)
    if best and best[2] < cur_err - tol:
        kept.append(best[0]); cur_err = best[2]; improved = True

w, err = fit(kept)
pred = sum(wi*fwd[i] for wi, i in zip(w, kept))
print("kept:", [periods[i] for i in kept], "w:", np.round(w,3), "MSE:", round(err,4))
for b, v in zip(bands, pred):
    print(b, round(float(v), 4))

# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.

# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.

               for t in range(1,10)] for b in bands])

fitted = (X @ coef).T            # trend + seasonal
resid = Y - fitted

h = 1.5
def smooth(y):
    out = np.zeros_like(y)

        A = np.column_stack([np.ones_like(t), t-t[i]])
        W = np.diag(w)
        beta = np.linalg.solve(A.T@W@A + 1e-8*np.eye(2), A.T@W@y)
        out[i] = beta[0]
    return out

mu, sd = sm.mean(axis=1, keepdims=True), sm.std(axis=1, keepdims=True)
Z = (sm - mu)/sd                 # prepared series

m, n = 3, 1
nb = T - m - n + 1               # 6 blocks

    k = len(idx)

                   method='SLSQP')

import numpy as np, pandas as pd, itertools
from scipy.optimize import minimize

df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')
bands = sorted(df['band'].unique())
T = 9
Y = np.array([[df[(df.band==b)&(df.period_id==f'P{t:02d}')]['mean_value'].iloc[0]
               for t in range(1,10)] for b in bands])

# preparation: standardize each band's observed series (match as observed, scaled)
mu, sd = Y.mean(axis=1, keepdims=True), Y.std(axis=1, keepdims=True)
Z = (Y - mu)/sd

m, n = 3, 1
nb = T - m - n + 1
match_win = Z[:, T-m:]
M = np.array([Z[:, i:i+m].ravel() for i in range(nb)])
F = np.array([Y[:, i+m] for i in range(nb)])   # forward month as observed

def fit_weights(idx):
    idx = list(idx)
    A = M[idx].T
    b = match_win.ravel()
    k = len(idx)
    def loss(w): return np.mean((A@w - b)**2)
    res = minimize(loss, np.ones(k)/k, bounds=[(0,None)]*k,
                   constraints={'type':'eq','fun': lambda w: w.sum()-1}, method='SLSQP')
    return res.x, loss(res.x)

best = None
for r in range(1, nb+1):
    for idx in itertools.combinations(range(nb), r):
        w, e = fit_weights(idx)
        if best is None or e < best[0]:
            best = (e, idx, w)
e, idx, w = best
print('kept blocks (start months):', [i+1 for i in idx], 'weights:', np.round(w,3), 'err:', round(e,5))

pred = sum(wi*F[i] for wi, i in zip(w, idx))
for b, v in zip(bands, pred):
    print(b, round(float(v), 4))

# Implement and run the synthetic historical control

The parcel's past is its comparison: blocks of its own earlier months are weighted to
reproduce its most recent months, and what followed those blocks becomes the forecast.
`references/method.md` describes the construction; every setting and every choice in it
is yours, made inside your program.

## Workflow

1. `python scripts/show_data.py` — the nine months, every band. The same data is in

   (P01–P09 in time order), `month` (YYYY-MM), `mean_value`.
2. Read `references/method.md`. Decide how to build the blocks, what to match, how to fit
   and constrain the weights, how to select blocks, and how to form the prediction.
3. Write `predict.py`. It reads `data.csv` and prints one line per band, `BAND VALUE`, the
   predicted mean value for the next month. numpy, scipy and pandas are available; nothing
   outside this directory is, and there is no network.
4. Run `python predict.py`. Fix what fails; run again. Every run is recorded.
5. Finish by writing `answer.json`:

# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.

from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd

LB = Path(".")
FEATURES_CSV = LB / "data.csv"
HER10_SITES = LB / "none.csv"

SD_TOL = 1e-8


def disp(band):
    return "VV-VH" if band == "VV_minus_VH" else band


def undisp(band):
    return "VV_minus_VH" if band == "VV-VH" else band


def _calendar():
    d = pd.read_csv(FEATURES_CSV)
    months = dict(zip(d.period_id, d.month))
    cal = {int(p[1:]): m for p, m in months.items()}
    y, mo = map(int, cal[max(cal)].split("-"))
    mo += 1
    if mo == 13:
        y, mo = y + 1, 1
    cal[max(cal) + 1] = f"{y:04d}-{mo:02d}"
    return cal


CALENDAR = _calendar()


def sensor_of(bands):
    return "sentinel1" if "VV" in set(bands) else "sentinel2"


def wide_from_data(path=FEATURES_CSV):
    """data.csv (band, period_id, month, mean_value) -> the wide frame lb_her_panel.panel_from_wide expects."""
    d = pd.read_csv(path)
    sensor = sensor_of(d.band.unique())
    w = d.pivot(index=["period_id", "month"], columns="band", values="mean_value").reset_index()
    w.columns = [c if c in ("period_id", "month") else f"mean_{undisp(c)}" for c in w.columns]
    w["sensor"] = sensor
    w["site_id"] = "site"
    w["seq"] = w.period_id.str[1:].astype(int)
    return w.sort_values("seq").reset_index(drop=True), sensor

# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.

from scipy.optimize import nnls

df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')
bands = sorted(df.band.unique())
months = ['P%02d'%i for i in range(1,10)]
Y = np.array([[df[(df.band==b)&(df.period_id==p)].mean_value.iloc[0] for p in months] for b in bands]) # bands x 9

m, n = 3, 1
nb = 9 - m - n + 1  # 6 blocks
# block i: matching months i..i+m-1, forward month i+m

F = np.array([Y[:, i+m].ravel() for i in range(nb)]).T     # bands x nb
target = Y[:, 9-m:].ravel()                                # matching window P07-P09

best = None
for r in range(1, nb+1):
    for sub in itertools.combinations(range(nb), r):
        w, _ = nnls(M[:, sub], target)
        if w.sum() <= 0: continue
        w = w / w.sum()
        err = np.mean((M[:, sub] @ w - target)**2)
        if best is None or err < best[0]:

err, sub, w = best
pred = F[:, sub] @ w
for b, v in zip(bands, pred):

# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.

Y = np.array([[df[(df.band==b)&(df.period_id==p)].mean_value.iloc[0] for p in periods] for b in bands]) # bands x 9

# preparation: remove annual sine/cosine after detrending with low-order (linear) trend
X = np.zeros((9,0))
prep = np.zeros_like(Y)
for i in range(len(bands)):
    y = Y[i]
    # design: trend, sin, cos (annual cycle ~ 12 months)
    D = np.column_stack([np.ones(9), t, np.sin(2*np.pi*t/12), np.cos(2*np.pi*t/12)])
    beta, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(D, y, rcond=None)
    r = y - D@beta
    # local-linear Gaussian kernel smoothing, bandwidth h=1.5
    h = 1.5
    sm = np.zeros(9)
    for k in range(9):
        w = np.exp(-0.5*((t-k)/h)**2)
        Dk = np.column_stack([np.ones(9), t-k])
        W = np.diag(w)
        b = np.linalg.solve(Dk.T@W@Dk + 1e-8*np.eye(2), Dk.T@W@r)
        sm[k] = b[0]
    sm = sm - sm.mean()
    sd = sm.std()
    prep[i] = sm/sd if sd>1e-9 else sm

m, n = 3, 1
nb = 9-m-n+1
blocks = [list(range(s, s+m)) for s in range(nb)]
forwards = [s+m for s in range(nb)]  # index of first forward month
match_win = list(range(9-m, 9))

M = np.array([[prep[i][j] for j in blk] for blk in blocks])  # blocks x m (per band stacked)
# build target vector: bands stacked
def block_vec(bi):
    return np.concatenate([prep[i][blocks[bi]] for i in range(len(bands))])
target = np.concatenate([prep[i][match_win] for i in range(len(bands))])
B = np.array([block_vec(b) for b in range(nb)])

best = None
for r in range(1, nb+1):
    for sub in itertools.combinations(range(nb), r):
        A = B[list(sub)].T
        w, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(A, target, rcond=None)
        w = np.clip(w, 0, None)  # nonnegative
        w = w/w.sum() if w.sum()>0 else w
        err = np.mean((B[list(sub)].T@w - target)**2)
        if best is None or err < best[0]-1e-12:
            best = (err, sub, w)
err, sub, w = best
print("kept blocks:", sub, "weights:", np.round(w,3), "match MSE:", err)

# prediction: weighted combination of first forward month, observed values
pred_obs = np.zeros(len(bands))
for k, bi in enumerate(sub):
    pred_obs += w[k]*Y[:, forwards[bi]]

# also prepared-space prediction with inverse transform, average with observed-space
# prepared-space: weighted combo of prepared forward values, then undo standardization,
# add back seasonal term for target month index t=9
pred_prep = np.zeros(len(bands))
for k, bi in enumerate(sub):
    pred_prep += w[k]*prep[:, forwards[bi]]
for i in range(len(bands)):
    y = Y[i]
    D = np.column_stack([np.ones(9), t, np.sin(2*np.pi*t/12), np.cos(2*np.pi*t/12)])
    beta, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(D, y, rcond=None)
    r = y - D@beta
    sm = r  # unsmoothed residual for scale/mean recovery approx
    mu, sd = sm.mean(), sm.std()
    D10 = np.array([1, 9, np.sin(2*np.pi*9/12), np.cos(2*np.pi*9/12)])
    pred_prep[i] = (pred_prep[i]*sd + mu) + D10@beta

pred = 0.5*pred_obs + 0.5*pred_prep
out = {b: round(float(v),4) for b,v in zip(bands, pred)}
for b,v in out.items(): print(b, v)
json.dump({"prediction": out, "rationale": "Synthetic historical control: bands prepared (annual sin/cos removed after linear trend, Gaussian local-linear smoothing h=1.5, standardized), m=3 matching window (P07-P09), n=1 forward month, 6 overlapping blocks, exhaustive nonnegative least-squares weight search over all subsets, prediction = weighted combination of forward months in observed space blended 50/50 with prepared-space prediction (seasonal term added back)."}, open('answer.json','w'), indent=1)
EOF
python predict.py

# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.

# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.

# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.

      f"{len(w)} consecutive calendar months. Bands: {', '.join(lb.disp(b) for b in bands)}.")
for _, r in w.iterrows():

import pandas as pd

LB = Path(".")
FEATURES_CSV = LB / "data.csv"
HER10_SITES = LB / "none.csv"
SENSORS = ("sentinel1", "sentinel2")
BANDS = {"sentinel1": ["VV", "VH", "VV_minus_VH"], "sentinel2": ["B2", "B3", "B4", "B8", "B11", "B12", "NDVI", "NDWI"]}
DECIMALS = {"sentinel2": 3, "sentinel1": 2}

SD_TOL = 1e-8


def disp(band):
    return "VV-VH" if band == "VV_minus_VH" else band


def undisp(band):
    return "VV_minus_VH" if band == "VV-VH" else band


def _calendar():
    d = pd.read_csv(FEATURES_CSV)
    months = dict(zip(d.period_id, d.month))
    cal = {int(p[1:]): m for p, m in months.items()}
    y, mo = map(int, cal[max(cal)].split("-"))
    mo += 1
    if mo == 13:
        y, mo = y + 1, 1
    cal[max(cal) + 1] = f"{y:04d}-{mo:02d}"
    return cal


CALENDAR = _calendar()


def sensor_of(bands):
    return "sentinel1" if "VV" in set(bands) else "sentinel2"


def wide_from_data(path=FEATURES_CSV):
    """data.csv (band, period_id, month, mean_value) -> the wide frame lb_her_panel.panel_from_wide expects."""
    d = pd.read_csv(path)
    sensor = sensor_of(d.band.unique())
    w = d.pivot(index=["period_id", "month"], columns="band", values="mean_value").reset_index()
    w.columns = [c if c in ("period_id", "month") else f"mean_{undisp(c)}" for c in w.columns]
    w["sensor"] = sensor
    w["site_id"] = "site"
    w["seq"] = w.period_id.str[1:].astype(int)
    return w.sort_values("seq").reset_index(drop=True), sensor

Blocks of m=3 consecutive months (matching part) plus the 1 month that
followed (forward part), sliding monthly: 6 blocks. Matching window is the
parcel's most recent m months (P07-P09). All 8 bands are stacked so one set
of non-negative block weights serves every band. Weights minimize MSE of the
weighted matching parts vs the matching window; blocks are selected stepwise
(keep best single block, then add one at a time while error falls by more
than a tolerance). Prediction = same weighted combination of each kept
block's first forward month, as observed.
"""
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

M, N = 3, 1          # matching length, forward length
TOL = 1e-6           # stepwise improvement tolerance

d = pd.read_csv("data.csv")
w = d.pivot(index="period_id", columns="band", values="mean_value").sort_index()
bands = list(w.columns)
Y = w.to_numpy()                      # 9 x 8, P01..P09
T = Y.shape[0]
nb = T - M - N + 1                    # number of blocks

# block i: matching rows i..i+M-1, forward row i+M
match_blocks = [Y[i:i+M].ravel() for i in range(nb)]
fwd = np.array([Y[i+M] for i in range(nb)])   # first forward month per block
target = Y[T-M:].ravel()                       # matching window, stacked

X = np.array(match_blocks).T                   # (M*8) x nb

def mse(idx):
    A = X[:, idx]
    # non-negative least squares via scipy
    from scipy.optimize import nnls
    coef, _ = nnls(A, target)
    r = A @ coef - target
    return float(r @ r) / len(target), coef

# stepwise selection
best_idx, best_err = None, np.inf
for i in range(nb):
    e, _ = mse([i])
    if e < best_err:
        best_err, best_idx = e, [i]
while True:
    improved = False
    for i in range(nb):
        if i in best_idx:
            continue
        e, _ = mse(best_idx + [i])
        if e < best_err - TOL:
            best_err, best_idx = e, best_idx + [i]
            improved = True
    if not improved:
        break

_, coef = mse(best_idx)
pred = np.zeros(len(bands))
for k, i in enumerate(best_idx):
    pred += coef[k] * fwd[i]

for b, v in zip(bands, pred):
    print(f"{b} {v:.6f}")
print(f"# kept blocks (start month index): {best_idx}, weights: {np.round(coef,4)}, match MSE: {best_err:.6f}")
EOF

# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.

    rem = resid - seas

    h = 2.0
    sm = np.zeros(9)
    for i in range(9):

        W = np.diag(w)

From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive

and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single

tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is

# Implement and run the synthetic historical control

The parcel's past is its comparison: blocks of its own earlier months are weighted to
reproduce its most recent months, and what followed those blocks becomes the forecast.
`references/method.md` describes the construction; every setting and every choice in it
is yours, made inside your program.

## Workflow

1. `python scripts/show_data.py` — the nine months, every band. The same data is in
   `data.csv` in this directory: one row per band per month, columns `band`, `period_id`
   (P01–P09 in time order), `month` (YYYY-MM), `mean_value`.
2. Read `references/method.md`. Decide how to build the blocks, what to match, how to fit
   and constrain the weights, how to select blocks, and how to form the prediction.
3. Write `predict.py`. It reads `data.csv` and prints one line per band, `BAND VALUE`, the
   predicted mean value for the next month. numpy, scipy and pandas are available; nothing
   outside this directory is, and there is no network.
4. Run `python predict.py`. Fix what fails; run again. Every run is recorded.
5. Finish by writing `answer.json`:
   ```json
   {"prediction": {"<band>": <value>, ...}, "rationale": "<what the program does and why>"}
   ```

steps.output:
# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.

# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.

from scipy.optimize import minimize

df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')
bands = sorted(df.band.unique())

Y = np.array([[df[(df.band==b)&(df.period_id==p)].mean_value.iloc[0] for p in periods] for b in bands])

mu = Y.mean(axis=1, keepdims=True); sd = Y.std(axis=1, keepdims=True)

blocks = [Z[:, s:s+m].ravel() for s in range(nb)]
fwd = [Z[:, s+m] for s in range(nb)]  # first forward month per band
target = Z[:, 9-m:].ravel()

def fit(subset):
    idx = list(subset)
    A = np.array([blocks[i] for i in idx]).T
    k = len(idx)

    cons = {'type':'eq','fun': lambda w: w.sum()-1}
    res = minimize(loss, np.ones(k)/k, bounds=[(0,1)]*k, constraints=cons, method='SLSQP')
    return res.fun, res.x, idx

best = None
for r in range(1, nb+1):
